Smooth Gaussian white noise curves

Source: R/smooth_gaussian_curves.R
smooth_gaussian_curves.Rd

Smooths the curves in a matrix produced by gaussian_swn(), then shifts and scales them to the requested mean and standard deviation. The same input data can be passed with different fwhm values to compare smoothness.

Usage

smooth_gaussian_curves(data, mu, sig, fwhm)

Arguments

data

A finite numeric matrix with evaluation points in rows and curves in columns, such as the output of gaussian_swn().

mu

A finite number, or a numeric vector with one target mean per evaluation point. A scalar is used at every point and for every curve.

sig

A positive finite number, or a numeric vector with one target standard deviation per evaluation point. A scalar is used at every point and for every curve.

fwhm

Positive finite scalar giving the full width at half maximum used for smoothing.

Value

A numeric matrix with the same dimensions as data: evaluation points in rows and curves in columns.

Examples

set.seed(123)
noise <- gaussian_swn(number_of_curves = 3, num_points = 100)
smooth_2 <- smooth_gaussian_curves(noise, mu = 0, sig = 1, fwhm = 2)
smooth_8 <- smooth_gaussian_curves(noise, mu = 0, sig = 1, fwhm = 8)
dim(smooth_2) # 100 3
#> [1] 100   3
dim(smooth_8) # 100 3
#> [1] 100   3

# The target mean and SD can vary across evaluation points.
smooth_varied <- smooth_gaussian_curves(
  noise,
  mu = seq(-1, 1, length.out = nrow(noise)),
  sig = seq(0.5, 1.5, length.out = nrow(noise)),
  fwhm = 4
)
